evals.prompt: Interrogate the proposed pagination change in the supplied pager-service project. Determine whether the change is justified, explainable, correct, and maintainable. Do not edit anything unless I approve a proposal.
evals.expected_output: A panel report that covers the boundary change, challenges the slicing rationale, identifies any correctness and test implications with evidence, and proposes rather than applies changes.
expectations: The report explains that Python slicing excludes the end index and that the proposed expression returns one fewer item than page_size.
The report identifies the missing regression coverage for actual page contents.
The report includes a questioner second-pass classification for every defender answer, a defender self-assessment, and an independent judge verdict with evidence.

The workflow uses persistent role contexts when the host supports them and treats fresh isolated follow-up agents with complete accumulated packets as a supported fallback rather than blocking when continuation is unavailable.
The report proposes necessary code or test changes without applying them and explicitly requests approval before editing.

evals.prompt: Interrogate the supplied directory-service documentation-only change. Determine whether it is justified, explainable, correct, and maintainable, but be strict about whether any additional explanation is actually warranted. Do not edit anything unless I approve a proposal.
evals.expected_output: A restrained panel report that covers the change, finds no material question or defect, avoids proposing tutorial comments or unrelated refactoring, and concludes that the change is defensible.
expectations: The report recognizes that the patch has no behavioral effect.
The report concludes that no additional comment, documentation, test, or refactoring is warranted.
The report records coverage without manufacturing a subsystem tutorial or speculative concern.
The report concludes that the change is defensible and does not modify the project.

evals.prompt: Interrogate the proposed refund event handler in the supplied event-service project. Treat event acknowledgement, amount-unit conversion, and per-handler observability as three user-specified semantic units. Determine whether the change is justified, explainable, correct, and maintainable. Do not edit anything unless I approve a proposal.
evals.expected_output: A complete semantic inventory and panel exchange that checks the event acknowledgement contract, amount units, and observability conventions; verifies claims against surrounding files; and proposes evidence-backed changes without applying them.
expectations: The report identifies that the handler fails to acknowledge, reject, or dead-letter the event as required by the handler contract.
The report identifies that amountMinor is already in minor units and multiplying it by 100 is incorrect.
The report identifies the missing per-handler observability metric.
The change inventory preserves the three user-specified semantic units, identifies them as user-specified, and accounts for any remaining diff behavior without silently changing their boundaries.
A semantic unit may produce multiple independently tracked questions when it contains distinct material explanation or correctness gaps.

The report verifies claims against surrounding repository files and includes a questioner second-pass classification for every defender answer, a defender self-assessment, and an independent judge verdict.
The report proposes necessary changes without applying them and explicitly requests approval before editing.
